review.plain: Making, mending or possessing tools designed for breaking into buildings or safes, or a master key for motor vehicles, with intent to use them for crime is punishable by up to 10 years in state prison.
acts: makes or mends, or begins to make or mend
has in his possession, an engine, machine, tool or implement adapted and designed for cutting through, forcing or breaking open a building, room, vault, safe or other depository
has in his possession a master key designed to fit more than one motor vehicle

penalties.penalty: Up to 10 years in state prison, or a fine of up to $1,000 and up to 2½ years in jail

crimes.act: Makes or mends, or begins to make or mend, or has in his possession, an engine, machine, tool or implement adapted and designed for cutting through, forcing or breaking open a building, room, vault, safe or other depository
conditions: The item is an engine, machine, tool or implement adapted and designed for cutting through, forcing or breaking open a building, room, vault, safe or other depository
knowledge: Knowing the same to be adapted and designed for the purpose aforesaid
intent: In order to steal therefrom money or other property, or to commit any other crime
With intent to use or employ or allow the same to be used or employed for such purpose

crimes.act: Has in his possession a master key designed to fit more than one motor vehicle
intent: With intent to use or employ the same to steal a motor vehicle or other property therefrom

review.plain: A person employed in the commonwealth's treasury who commits a fraud or embezzlement there faces a fine of up to $2,000 or state prison for life or any term of years.

crimes.act: Commits a fraud or embezzlement therein

fraudulently takes or secretes with intent so to do, effects or property which belong to or are in possession of said county, city or town

penalties.penalty: Up to 10 years in state prison, or a fine of up to $1,000 and up to 2 years in jail

intent: With intent so to do (when taking or secreting)

conditions: Applies whether or not intrusted with the custody thereof

crimes.act: Aids, counsels or procures such larceny to be committed
crimes.who: Any person

crimes.act: Receives or permits the receipt of any deposit
crimes.who: An officer or employee of a bank

review.plain: A bank liquidating agent, commissioner's employee, or court-appointed receiver who embezzles or misapplies property in their possession is guilty of larceny and faces up to 10 years in state prison.

review.plain: A broker or corporate broker-officer who embezzles or fraudulently converts money, stock or security entrusted with written investment directions faces up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: embezzles or fraudulently converts such money, stock or security, or any part thereof, or the proceeds or any part of the proceeds thereof

conditions: Intrusted, solely or jointly, with money, stock or security for the payment of money, with a direction in writing to invest, dispose of, apply, pay or deliver it
Acts in violation of good faith and contrary to the terms of such direction
crimes.who: A broker, or officer, manager or agent of a corporation doing the business of brokers

review.plain: A trustee, guardian, conservator, executor or administrator who embezzles or fraudulently converts property held for another or for a public or charitable purpose faces up to 10 years in state prison.
acts: embezzles or fraudulently converts or appropriates money, goods or property held or possessed by him for the use or benefit, either wholly or partially, of some other person or for a public or charitable purpose
otherwise fraudulently disposes of or destroys such property

penalties.penalty: Up to 10 years in state prison, or a fine of up to $2,000 and up to 2 years in jail

crimes.act: Embezzles or fraudulently converts or appropriates money, goods or property held or possessed by him for the use or benefit, either wholly or partially, of some other person or for a public or charitable purpose, to or for his own use or benefit or to or for the use or benefit of any other person or for any other purpose
crimes.who: A trustee under an express trust created by a deed, will or other instrument in writing, or a guardian, conservator, executor or administrator, or any person upon or to whom such a trust has devolved or come

crimes.act: Otherwise fraudulently disposes of or destroys such property
crimes.who: A trustee under an express trust created by a deed, will or other instrument in writing, or a guardian, conservator, executor or administrator, or any person upon or to whom such a trust has devolved or come

review.plain: An officer, agent, clerk or servant of a voluntary association who embezzles or fraudulently converts its property is guilty of larceny.

crimes.act: Embezzles or fraudulently converts, or fraudulently takes or secretes, effects or property which belong to such association or society, or which have come to his possession or are under his care by virtue of his office or employment

crimes.who: An officer, agent, clerk or servant of a voluntary association or society

conditions: The property may be the subject of larceny
The property belongs to an organization of the volunteer militia, post of the Grand Army of the Republic, or other voluntary association
intent: With intent to embezzle or fraudulently convert (when secreting)

penalties.penalty: Guilty of simple larceny; penalty not set in this section

consequences: Applies although he is a member of the organization or association and entitled to an interest in its property

buys, receives or aids in the concealment of property
obtains or exerts control over property in the custody of any law enforcement agency, or any individual acting on behalf of a law enforcement agency

penalties.penalty: Up to 2½ years in the house of correction or a fine of up to $3,000, if the value of the property does not exceed $1,200 and it is a first offense

penalties.if: The value of the property does not exceed $1,200 and it is a second or subsequent offense
penalties.penalty: Up to 2½ years in the house of correction, or up to 5 years in state prison, or a fine of up to $5,000, or both a fine and imprisonment

penalties.if: The value of the property exceeds $1,200
penalties.penalty: Up to 2½ years in the house of correction, or up to 5 years in state prison, or a fine of up to $5,000, or both a fine and imprisonment

knowledge: Knowing it to have been stolen or embezzled

intent: Intends to deprive its rightful owner permanently of the use and enjoyment of said property

review.plain: Lets crimes under this chapter committed in different counties or court districts be charged and prosecuted in any court having jurisdiction of at least one of them, if they could otherwise be joined for trial.
Provides that a person on a first conviction for receiving stolen property who shows the theft was simple larceny and makes full restitution cannot be imprisoned in state prison.
Anyone convicted of receiving stolen property after a prior like conviction, or of three or more such acts at one sitting, is a common receiver of stolen goods, with up to 10 years in state prison.

consequences: Adjudged a common receiver of stolen or embezzled goods

knowledge: Knowing it to have been stolen or embezzled

review.plain: Wilfully and mischievously taking or using someone's boat, non-motor vehicle or draught animal without consent is punishable by up to 6 months in prison or a $300 fine.

takes, drives, rides or uses any draught animal which is the property of another
